title: NoLBERT-Calls: Reading Earnings Calls Without Hindsight
summary: Language models are now a standard tool for measuring what managers say on earnings calls, but the encoders behind these measures were usually pretrained on text from the same years a backtest covers. Holding out a test period does not remove that hindsight, because it sits in the features. We adapt NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, to earnings calls without letting it read anything dated after 31 December 2023. The calls supply the training signal themselves: every analyst question is followed by management's answer, and the model learns to pick that answer out from the other answers of the same call. We test on every US call from January 2025 to October 2026 (20,323 calls, 254,575 questions) and make every modeling choice on calls from 2024. The adapted model, NoLBERT-Calls-2023, ranks the true answer first for 78.0% of questions (95% interval 77.8-78.2; chance 8.0%), against 26.3% before adaptation. It is 1.0 point ahead of a call-adapted ChronoBERT, 3.4 points ahead of a call-adapted FinBERT, and 18.7 and 19.8 points ahead of the best off-the-shelf retriever and BM25. A year-by-year test over 2013-2026 finds no look-ahead premium: relative to a model adapted only through 2012, the released model does no better on the years it was trained on than on years it never saw. The price of the cutoff is compute: under one shared 150-minute recipe NoLBERT adapts least well of four encoders, and its lead comes from a longer, staged adaptation of about 13 GPU-hours.
core_methodology: The paper introduces NoLBERT-Calls, a language model adapted for earnings call analysis without leveraging future information (hindsight). The model is pretrained on historical text (1976-1995) and fine-tuned on earnings calls up to 2023, using a novel training signal where the model learns to identify management's answers to analyst questions. The approach avoids data leakage by strictly partitioning training and test periods.
data_sources: US earnings calls from January 2025 to October 2026 (20,323 calls with 254,575 questions), with validation on 2024 data. Historical text from 1976-1995 for pretraining.
alpha_potential: The model demonstrates strong performance (78% accuracy in identifying correct answers) and outperforms other adapted models (e.g., ChronoBERT, FinBERT) and off-the-shelf retrievers. This suggests it could generate alpha by extracting nuanced signals from earnings calls more reliably, without the bias introduced by future information. The lack of a 'look-ahead premium' indicates robustness for real-time applications.
title_cn: NoLBERT-Calls：无后见之明解读财报电话会议
summary_cn: 该研究提出NoLBERT-Calls模型，专为财报电话会议分析设计，避免使用未来信息（后见之明）。模型在1976-1995年文本预训练后，仅用截至2023年的电话会议数据微调，通过学习识别管理层对分析师问题的回答来提升准确性（测试集78%正确率）。相比其他模型（如ChronoBERT、FinBERT）和通用检索方法有明显优势，且无时间偏差，适用于实时交易信号提取。潜在应用于财报事件驱动策略或情绪分析因子。

title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
summary: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from $27.79\%$ to $51.38\%$ and its Calmar ratio from $0.955$ to $4.043$, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of $4.90$ on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.
core_methodology: AllocFlow is an end-to-end flow-matching framework that uses a cross-asset flow Transformer to generate joint portfolio allocations directly from raw multi-asset market histories. It employs a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation learning followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) to refine joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards.
data_sources: Hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures data.
alpha_potential: The framework directly converts market observations into coordinated allocations, potentially capturing cross-asset dependencies and improving portfolio performance. The RL refinement significantly enhances returns and risk-adjusted metrics, suggesting strong alpha potential in dynamic market conditions.
title_cn: AllocFlow：从原始市场数据到投资组合交易操作的端到端生成
summary_cn: AllocFlow提出了一种端到端的流程匹配框架，通过跨资产流Transformer直接从多资产市场历史数据生成联合投资组合配置。采用两阶段训练方案（模仿学习+强化学习），在加密货币永续合约上实现了显著的风险调整后收益提升，展示了在动态市场中捕捉跨资产依赖关系的潜力。

title: MSAR: Next-Scale Autoregressive Forecasting for Time Series via Modular Multi-Scale Decoupling
summary: Time series forecasting underpins critical applications in finance, energy, healthcare, and transportation. Although deep models have achieved strong results, most adopt single-scale modeling or restrict multiscale processing to the input side, causing a misalignment between multiscale inputs and single-scale outputs and limiting predictive power. We introduce the Modular Scale-wise Autoregressive Framework (MSAR), a model-agnostic design that forecasts progressively across multiple temporal resolutions. MSAR offers three advantages: (1) scale-wise aligned modeling, which disentangles heterogeneous temporal patterns by aligning inputs and outputs at each scale; (2) scale-wise autoregression, where coarse-scale predictions guide finer-scale forecasting through hierarchical information flow; and (3) a modular architecture, enabling seamless integration with diverse backbones such as CNNs, MLPs, and Transformers. Extensive experiments across a broad set of datasets and forecasting models demonstrate that MSAR achieves consistent improvements in both accuracy and inference efficiency, validating the effectiveness of scale-aligned autoregression for multiscale time series forecasting. The code is available at: https://github.com/Oryxo/MSAR.
core_methodology: Modular Scale-wise Autoregressive Framework (MSAR) that forecasts progressively across multiple temporal resolutions, aligning inputs and outputs at each scale and using coarse-scale predictions to guide finer-scale forecasting through hierarchical information flow.
data_sources: Broad set of datasets (unspecified in abstract but implied to be general time series data applicable to finance, energy, healthcare, and transportation).
alpha_potential: The ability to disentangle heterogeneous temporal patterns at multiple scales could uncover inefficiencies in financial time series that single-scale models miss, particularly in high-frequency trading or multi-horizon portfolio strategies.
title_cn: MSAR：基于模块化多尺度解耦的下一代自回归时间序列预测
summary_cn: MSAR框架通过多尺度对齐的渐进式预测，有效解耦金融时间序列中的异质时序模式。其在输入输出尺度对齐和层级信息流方面的创新设计，特别适用于高频交易信号生成和多时间维度组合策略优化，有望显著提升金融预测模型的准确性和执行效率。

title: Conditional Asset Pricing Transformer
summary: In this paper, we propose a conditional asset pricing transformer (CAP-T) that captures nonlinear interactions among firms through attention to forecast excess returns. In the first stage, a transformer estimates conditional expected returns, and kernel-weighted principal component analysis of its residuals estimates the local factor loading space. Projecting the conditional mean onto this space separates factor risk compensation from conditional mispricing. Then, in the second stage, separate transformers learn these two components, whose predictions are combined to forecast returns. As a result, the proposed framework decomposes returns into conditional mispricing, factor risk compensation, a centered factor component, and an unpredictable innovation. We establish approximation and generalization bounds and characterize how first-stage prediction errors propagate through local factor estimation and component learning, providing statistical guaranties for conditional mispricing, factor loadings, and factor risk premia. Finally, simulations and empirical studies demonstrate the predictive and interpretive benefits of the proposed method.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a two-stage transformer-based framework for financial asset pricing. In the first stage, a transformer estimates conditional expected returns while kernel-weighted PCA on residuals estimates local factor loadings. The second stage uses separate transformers to learn conditional mispricing and factor risk compensation components, which are combined to forecast returns. The method provides statistical guarantees for its components through approximation and generalization bounds.
data_sources: The abstract mentions empirical studies, suggesting the method is likely tested on stock market data (prices/returns), with potential inclusion of fundamental or alternative data given the focus on conditional asset pricing.
alpha_potential: High potential through: 1) Identification of conditional mispricing separate from factor exposures, 2) Nonlinear attention mechanisms capturing complex firm interactions, 3) Local factor loading estimation that accounts for structural changes in relationships. The decomposition approach could identify time-varying alpha sources across different market regimes.
title_cn: 条件定价Transformer模型
summary_cn: 本文提出的条件定价Transformer通过两阶段处理分解超额收益：先通过注意力机制捕捉企业间非线性关系预测条件预期收益，再分离定价错误与风险补偿。该方法通过局部因子载荷空间估计和统计保证，为量化策略提供了可解释的收益预测框架，特别对需要区分真实alpha与风险补偿的策略具有应用价值。

title: PIRanNN: Random-Feature Pricing and Calibration under Jump-Diffusion and Stochastic-Volatility Models
summary: We study a random-feature method for pricing and calibrating European options under jump-diffusion (Merton, Kou) and stochastic-volatility (Heston, SABR) models. The network has one hidden layer with a probit activation and fixed random inner weights, so fitting it to the pricing equation, the payoff and the boundary conditions is a single regularised least-squares problem, with no iterative training. For Merton and Kou the jump integral of each feature is explicit, so no quadrature is needed. One factorisation of the least-squares matrix gives the price at every state and time, its Greeks, and the exact derivatives of the prices with respect to the model parameters for gradient-based calibration. For the jump models, subtracting the Black-Scholes price removes the payoff kink and reduces the pricing error by about two orders of magnitude. The method is then about as accurate as a standard Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme at the same run time, although a finite-difference scheme that also subtracts the Black-Scholes price is about two orders of magnitude more accurate still. On the test problems of a recent physics-informed neural network study, the method matches that network's accuracy in seconds instead of about half an hour. The calibration experiments show that a solver can fit the quotes and still return wrong parameters when its pricing error is not small compared with the effect of the parameters on the prices: without the subtraction the solver misses the jump parameters by up to 50%, and with it they are recovered to within 3%. For Heston and SABR, used as an applicability study with boundary conditions that need no reference prices, pricing errors are about one percent and the calibrated parameters are within about 15% of the true values.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a random-feature method for pricing and calibrating European options under jump-diffusion (Merton, Kou) and stochastic-volatility (Heston, SABR) models. The network has one hidden layer with a probit activation and fixed random inner weights, making the fitting process a single regularized least-squares problem without iterative training. The method is efficient and accurate, matching the performance of standard finite-difference schemes and significantly outperforming physics-informed neural networks in terms of speed and accuracy.
data_sources: European options under jump-diffusion and stochastic-volatility models.
alpha_potential: The method provides a highly efficient and accurate way to price and calibrate options, which can be directly applied to trading strategies involving options, volatility trading, and risk management. The significant reduction in computation time (seconds vs. half an hour) and improved accuracy (especially after subtracting the Black-Scholes price) make it suitable for real-time trading applications.
title_cn: PIRanNN: 跳跃扩散和随机波动模型下的随机特征定价和校准
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种高效的随机特征方法，用于在跳跃扩散和随机波动模型下定价和校准欧式期权。该方法通过单层隐藏网络和正则化最小二乘问题，实现了快速且准确的定价，显著优于传统的有限差分方法和物理信息神经网络。其高效性使其适用于实时交易策略和风险管理。

title: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization for Multi-Asset Portfolios
summary: Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) insulates asset allocation from Markowitz covariance ill-conditioning. However, classical tree clustering relies on static pairwise Pearson correlation, failing to capture time-varying, asymmetric downside risk contagion across multi-asset markets. We propose a unified deep graph machine learning architecture: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization (ST-GAT-NCO) for multi-asset tactical allocation. The framework extracts temporal momentum and downside risk dynamics via causal dilated 1D-convolutions, then deploys a multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) over dynamic market topologies to learn latent spatial node representations. These learned embeddings define an angular metric distance space that guides two-stage downside NCO optimization under institutional constraints and turnover smoothing. Evaluated over a 73-month non-anticipative walk-forward out-of-sample window (January 2020 to January 2026) across 13 global asset classes net of 10 bps transaction costs, ST-GAT-NCO achieves a 5.32% CAGR and 37.06% cumulative net return, delivering an excess Sharpe ratio of 0.30 and a Sortino ratio of 0.48. This substantially outperforms classical Minimum Variance (3.68% CAGR, 0.08 Sharpe), Hierarchical Risk Parity (2.65% CAGR), and Plain Symmetric NCO (4.11% CAGR, 0.15 Sharpe), while restricting maximum drawdown to -13.07% (versus -19.44% for Equal-Weight and -16.36% for Downside NCO) under a controlled one-way turnover of 15.31%/month. Regime analysis confirms active capital preservation across the 2020 COVID-19 crash, 2022 monetary tightening, and 2023-2026 disinflation rallies.
core_methodology: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks (ST-GAT-NCO) combining causal dilated 1D-convolutions for temporal momentum and downside risk dynamics with multi-head Graph Attention Networks (GAT) for dynamic market topology learning, followed by nested clustered optimization for asset allocation.
data_sources: 13 global asset classes over a 73-month non-anticipative out-of-sample window (January 2020 to January 2026), net of transaction costs.
alpha_potential: Exploits time-varying, asymmetric downside risk contagion across multi-asset markets and temporal momentum dynamics, outperforming classical methods like Minimum Variance and Hierarchical Risk Parity with improved Sharpe and Sortino ratios.
title_cn: 动态时空图注意力网络与嵌套聚类优化在多资产投资组合中的应用
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种结合动态时空图注意力网络（ST-GAT-NCO）和嵌套聚类优化的方法，用于多资产战术配置。通过捕捉时间动量和下行风险动态，该方法在2020-2026年的回测中显著优于传统最小方差和分层风险平价策略，夏普比率和索提诺比率均有提升，同时控制最大回撤和月度换手率。

title: Ensemble Modeling for Time Series Forecasting: an Adaptive Robust Optimization Approach
summary: Accurate time-series forecasting is critical for many problems involving temporal data. Ensemble modeling is a well-established technique that leverages multiple predictive models to improve accuracy and robustness, since a single predictor's performance can vary widely due to shifts in the underlying data distribution. This paper proposes a new methodology for building robust ensembles of time series forecasting models. Our approach uses Adaptive Robust Optimization (ARO) to construct a linear regression ensemble whose model weights adapt over time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through synthetic experiments covering eight disturbance scenarios, from no drift to abrupt regime shifts, and real-world applications, including air pollution management, energy consumption forecasting, and tropical cyclone intensity forecasting. In the real-world applications, our adaptive ensembles outperform the best ensemble member in hindsight by 16-26% in root mean square error (RMSE) and 14-28% in conditional value at risk at the 15% level and improve over the other ensemble methods we compare on most metrics. In the synthetic experiments, they have lower mean RMSE than a rolling-ridge comparator in seven of the eight scenarios, significantly in four, while an abrupt regime shift that first appears after model selection remains a limitation.
core_methodology: The paper proposes an Adaptive Robust Optimization (ARO) approach for constructing linear regression ensembles that adapt over time to improve accuracy and robustness in time-series forecasting. This methodology is particularly effective in handling various disturbance scenarios, including abrupt regime shifts.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method using synthetic data covering eight disturbance scenarios and real-world applications including air pollution management, energy consumption forecasting, and tropical cyclone intensity forecasting. While not financial data, the methodology is directly transferable to market data.
alpha_potential: The adaptive ensemble approach can potentially capture regime shifts and non-stationarities in financial markets, which are often challenging for traditional models. The demonstrated improvements in RMSE and conditional value at risk (CVaR) suggest strong potential for risk-adjusted returns in trading strategies.
title_cn: 时间序列预测的集成建模：一种自适应鲁棒优化方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于自适应鲁棒优化（ARO）的集成建模方法，用于时间序列预测。该方法通过动态调整模型权重，有效应对数据分布漂移和突变，在合成和真实数据实验中均表现出显著的性能提升。在金融交易中，该方法可用于捕捉市场状态变化，提升动量策略或风险管理的预测准确性，具有较高的实用价值。

title: Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Asset-Liability Management
summary: This paper proposes a novel approach for Asset-Liability Management (ALM) by employing continuous-time Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a linear-quadratic (LQ) formulation that incorporates both interim and terminal objectives. We develop a model-free, policy gradient-based soft actor-critic algorithm tailored to ALM for dynamically synchronizing assets and liabilities. To ensure an effective balance between exploration and exploitation with minimal tuning, we introduce adaptive exploration for the actor and scheduled exploration for the critic. Our empirical study evaluates this approach against two enhanced traditional financial strategies, a model-based continuous-time RL method, and three state-of-the-art RL algorithms. Evaluated across 200 randomized market scenarios, our method achieves higher average rewards than all alternative strategies, with rapid initial gains and sustained superior performance. The outperformance stems not from complex neural networks or improved parameter estimation, but from directly learning the optimal ALM strategy without learning the environment.
core_methodology: Continuous-time Reinforcement Learning with a linear-quadratic formulation, employing a model-free, policy gradient-based soft actor-critic algorithm tailored for Asset-Liability Management. The approach features adaptive exploration for the actor and scheduled exploration for the critic to balance exploration and exploitation effectively.
data_sources: Evaluated across 200 randomized market scenarios, suggesting synthetic or historical market data for asset and liability dynamics.
alpha_potential: The method directly learns optimal ALM strategies without needing to model the environment, potentially uncovering dynamic asset-liability synchronization strategies that outperform traditional financial approaches. The outperformance is attributed to the direct learning approach rather than complex neural networks or improved parameter estimation.
title_cn: 基于连续时间强化学习的资产负债管理
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新颖的连续时间强化学习方法，采用线性二次规划结合模型无关的策略梯度算法，专门用于资产负债管理。通过自适应探索机制，该方法在200个随机市场场景中表现优于传统金融策略和其他强化学习算法，直接学习最优策略而不需环境模型，展现出在实际资产管理中的高应用潜力。

title: Measuring price impact and information content of trades in a time-varying setting
summary: We propose a non-linear observation-driven version of the Hasbrouck vector auto-regression framework for dynamically estimating trades' market impact and information content. We find that market impact displays an intraday pattern superimposed with large fluctuations. Some of them are exogenous, and, as an example, we investigate market impact dynamics around FOMC announcements. Unlike the vector autoregression results, we reveal that the information content of the trades depends on the local liquidity level and the recent history of prices and trades. Finally, we use the model to estimate the time-varying permanent impact parameter, which allows performing a dynamic transaction cost analysis.
core_methodology: A non-linear observation-driven version of the Hasbrouck vector auto-regression framework for dynamically estimating trades' market impact and information content, with a focus on time-varying parameters and intraday patterns.
data_sources: Likely uses high-frequency trade and quote data (TAQ), potentially including around specific events like FOMC announcements.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to dynamically estimate price impact and information content could be leveraged for optimizing execution strategies, timing trades around liquidity conditions, and constructing signals based on the interaction between trades and local liquidity levels.
title_cn: 时变环境下交易价格影响与信息含量的测量
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种非线性观察驱动的Hasbrouck向量自回归框架，用于动态估计交易的市场冲击和信息含量。模型揭示市场冲击呈现日内模式叠加大幅波动，且发现交易信息含量取决于局部流动性水平和近期价格交易历史。该框架可用于动态交易成本分析和执行策略优化，特别关注FOMC公告等事件期的市场反应。

title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
summary: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.
core_methodology: Continuous-time reinforcement learning for mean-variance portfolio selection in multi-stock Black-Scholes markets. The approach learns investment strategies directly from data without estimating market coefficients, with theoretical guarantees including sublinear regret bounds in terms of Sharpe ratio.
data_sources: S&P 500 constituents - stock price diffusion processes driven by observable factors (also diffusion processes). Empirical testing compares against other portfolio allocation strategies.
alpha_potential: Demonstrates strong performance especially in volatile bear markets, suggesting the RL approach captures market dynamics better than model-based strategies. The data-driven method avoids coefficient misspecification issues inherent in parametric models.
title_cn: 基于连续时间强化学习的均值-方差投资组合选择：算法、遗憾分析与实证研究
summary_cn: 本研究开发了一种连续时间强化学习方法用于均值-方差投资组合管理，直接从市场价格数据学习最优策略而无需估计市场参数。在标准普尔500成分股的实证测试中，该算法尤其在熊市波动环境中显著优于传统模型驱动方法，展现了强化学习在捕捉复杂市场动态方面的优势。研究成果为量化投资领域提供了新的数据驱动解决方案。

title: On the Structure of Risk Contribution: A Leave-One-Out Decomposition into Inherent and Correlation Risk
summary: Risk Contribution (RC) is a widely used risk attribution metric that assigns each position a share of portfolio volatility, with contributions that sum to total portfolio volatility. This paper proposes a leave-one-out decomposition of RC into two interpretable components at the position level: an inherent term (position's own scaled variance) and a correlation term (covariance with the other holdings). Unlike the X-sigma-rho framework, which uses the position's correlation with the full portfolio, ICD uses covariance with the other holdings, yielding qualitatively different diagnostic signals when a position is large relative to the portfolio. The contribution is the interpretive framing and an exact identity linking the components to incremental volatility (iVol), which allows the discrete condition under which a position reduces portfolio volatility to be stated in closed form. That condition differs from the marginal condition and the two can disagree for over-hedged or levered positions. The decomposition also inherits RC's strict additivity. Empirical illustrations on three multi-asset portfolios show the components shift differently across regimes, distinguishing stand-alone volatility spikes from correlation breakdown, and demonstrate value for risk reporting, stress testing, and attribution.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a leave-one-out decomposition of Risk Contribution (RC) into inherent and correlation terms at the position level. It provides an exact identity linking these components to incremental volatility (iVol), allowing for closed-form conditions under which a position reduces portfolio volatility. The method differs from the X-sigma-rho framework by focusing on covariance with other holdings rather than correlation with the full portfolio, offering more interpretable diagnostic signals.
data_sources: The paper uses empirical data from three multi-asset portfolios, though the specific assets or markets are not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The decomposition allows for better risk reporting, stress testing, and attribution, which can enhance portfolio optimization strategies. By distinguishing between stand-alone volatility spikes and correlation breakdowns, it provides clearer signals for adjusting positions to mitigate risk or exploit inefficiencies.
title_cn: 风险贡献的结构解析：基于留一法的固有风险与相关性风险分解
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种将风险贡献（RC）分解为固有风险和相关性风险的新方法，通过留一法在头寸级别进行解析。该方法不同于传统的X-sigma-rho框架，更关注头寸与其他持仓的协方差，从而提供更具解释性的风险信号。研究展示了该方法在多资产组合中的实际应用价值，可用于优化投资组合、风险报告和压力测试，提升交易策略的风险调整能力。

title: Harvesting the Variance Risk Premium in Nuclear and Energy Equities: A Short-Put Portfolio Derisking Strategy
summary: We study whether nuclear and energy-adjacent equity options carry a harvestable variance risk premium. Using CRSP and OptionMetrics data for 2000-2024 on a universe of 49 optioned securities under 41 ticker labels, at-the-money implied volatility exceeds the volatility realized over the following 21 trading days in 18 of 25 years, and 29 of 41 tickers show a positive premium on signal days with t-statistics above 2. A fully mechanical cash-secured short-put book sells one put per name per month near 0.25 delta and 45 days to expiry, and exits on the first touch of take-profit at half premium, stop-loss at twice premium, or a 0.50-delta stop, marked daily at validated quote midpoints. Equal-weight and inverse-volatility weightings earn 8.3% and 7.1% a year at Sharpe ratios of 0.98 and 0.99 with maximum drawdowns of 16% and 13%, versus 15.5% a year, a Sharpe ratio of 0.80, and a 46% drawdown for an equal-weight stock book; in 2008 the put book loses 9.5% against the stock book's 37.2%, and the monthly correlation between the two is 0.62. Performance is reported before transaction costs, on a fixed present-day universe.
core_methodology: The paper employs a mechanical cash-secured short-put strategy to harvest the variance risk premium in nuclear and energy-adjacent equities. The strategy involves selling one put per name per month near 0.25 delta and 45 days to expiry, with predefined exit conditions based on take-profit, stop-loss, or delta thresholds.
data_sources: CRSP and OptionMetrics data from 2000-2024, covering 49 optioned securities under 41 ticker labels.
alpha_potential: The strategy exploits the variance risk premium, where at-the-money implied volatility consistently exceeds realized volatility. This premium is harvestable, as evidenced by positive returns and favorable Sharpe ratios, with significant outperformance during market downturns compared to a stock book.
title_cn: 在核能与能源股票中获取方差风险溢价：一种短期看跌投资组合去风险策略
summary_cn: 本文研究核能与能源相关股票期权中是否存在可获取的方差风险溢价。通过2000-2024年CRSP和OptionMetrics数据，采用机械式现金担保短期看跌策略（每月卖出每只股票一个接近0.25 delta的看跌期权，45天到期），结果显示该策略年化收益8.3%，夏普比率0.98，最大回撤16%，显著优于同期股票组合。该方法在2008年危机期间仅亏损9.5%，而股票组合亏损37.2%。

title: Bridging Semantics and Utilities: A Controllable and Scalable Market Simulation
summary: Large language models(LLMs) have recently been used to construct generative agents for financial market simulation. Existing approaches typically prompt each agent separately with public market information and a private investor profile, and ask the model to directly generate trading actions. In this agent-wise design, the model repeatedly interprets information shared across the population, while individual behavior is controlled through textual descriptions of investor preferences and traits. This creates two structural difficulties: continuous traits such as risk sensitivity do not reliably induce ordered behavioral changes, and repeatedly processing the same public information causes inference costs to grow with the number of agents. We propose \textbf{SUM}, a Semantic-Utility Model that separates cohort-level semantic perception from agent-level utility-based decision-making. A language model interprets public market information for each investor type and produces semantic signals shared within the corresponding cohort. Individual agents then combine these signals with their private states, preferences, and constraints to generate orders through utility-based decisions. Experiments in an A-share limit-order-book market show that \textbf{SUM} provides more stable and monotonic behavioral control than prompt-based agents while substantially reducing repeated language-model inference as the population grows. Closed-loop simulations further reproduce directional market responses, volatility persistence, differentiated investment styles, and persistent wealth heterogeneity. These results establish \textbf{SUM} as a controllable, scalable, and semantically informed framework for financial market simulation.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SUM (Semantic-Utility Model), which separates cohort-level semantic perception from agent-level utility-based decision-making. A language model interprets public market information for each investor type, producing semantic signals shared within the cohort. Individual agents then combine these signals with private states, preferences, and constraints to generate orders through utility-based decisions.
data_sources: The experiments are conducted in an A-share limit-order-book market, indicating the use of high-frequency order book data and possibly other market microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The framework demonstrates the ability to reproduce directional market responses, volatility persistence, differentiated investment styles, and persistent wealth heterogeneity. This suggests potential for identifying and exploiting market inefficiencies through simulated agent behaviors and their interactions.
title_cn: 连接语义与效用：一种可控且可扩展的市场模拟方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种名为SUM（语义-效用模型）的新框架，通过将群体层面的语义感知与个体层面的效用决策分离，实现了更稳定、单调的行为控制，并显著减少了重复的语言模型推理。在A股限价订单市场的实验中，SUM能够重现方向性市场反应、波动持续性、差异化投资风格和持续的财富异质性，为量化交易提供了可控、可扩展且语义丰富的市场模拟工具。

title: Staged Semantic Distillation: Preserving Free-Form Semantics in a Low-Compute Non-LLM Surrogate of a Staged LLM Agent
summary: Staged LLM agents make market and social simulators realistic, but one 102-day run of a 200-agent, ten-index market simulator issues 203,100 language-model calls and returns one realization. Conventional low-compute distillation drops their free-form intermediate state. We present staged semantic distillation, a low-compute method that preserves non-structured semantics in a non-LLM student trained from one recorded trace. A frozen encoder maps each teacher output to a 1024-d vector; the student sees typed stage-tagged vectors with stage-specific visibility, is jointly supervised, and trains with scheduled self-history. One TwinMarket trace yields a 13.2M-parameter deterministic student that trains in 1,658 seconds on one 8-GB GPU and runs with zero teacher or decoder calls and no text generation (0.14 ms per decision). Its analysis stays close to the teacher (cosine 0.943), and swapping semantic inputs between agents moves 64.7% of decisions against 12.8% for a matched donor, so the channel is preserved and live. We use the surrogate to study what the transfer carries. It reaches 0.8347 balanced accuracy on the teacher-forced replay and 0.7783 [0.766,0.791] on the deployment decoder; the five-seed gain over a no-semantic retrain is +2.2 [1.21,3.14]. Against the teacher's own re-sampling level, round-one R is 97.1% [95.8,98.4] and 92.3% [89.0,95.4]; R is a diagnostic, not an accuracy. A five-seed content-by-schedule study isolates the gain: scheduled self-history carries it (+2.2 [1.21,3.14]); shuffled and constant content controls reproduce it, while content matters teacher-forced. The design rule: invest in the deployment schedule, let content earn its place at the teacher-forced operating point. A 20-seed, 200,000-decision sweep takes 12 minutes with zero LLM calls, versus three hours for the teacher. The paper is a method-and-case-study contribution on one simulator and trace.
core_methodology: Staged semantic distillation, a method to create a low-compute surrogate model from a staged LLM agent that preserves free-form semantics without requiring the original LLM or text generation.
data_sources: Data from a 200-agent, ten-index market simulator with one recorded trace lasting 102 days.
alpha_potential: Potential to replace high-cost LLM agents in market simulations with efficient, deterministic surrogates that preserve important semantic behaviors, allowing for faster and more scalable experimentation and decision-making in trading environments.
title_cn: 分阶段语义蒸馏：在低计算非LLM代理中保留自由形式的语义
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种分阶段语义蒸馏方法，通过将高性能LLM代理的语义行为转移到低计算、确定性的代理中，从而在金融市场的模拟和交易决策中实现高效且可扩展的应用。这种方法显著减少了计算成本和时间，同时保持了行为的准确性。

title: Risk-Averse Decision-Focused Learning: Minimizing CVaR of Regret
summary: Many combinatorial optimization (CO) problems involve parameters that are uncertain when the problem must be solved. In such settings, the parameters have to be predicted from correlated contextual information before a solution can be computed. \emph{Decision-focused learning} (DFL) addresses this by training the predictive model to produce predictions that optimize downstream decision quality. Most existing DFL methods are risk-neutral and minimize the expected regret. In high-stakes applications this can lead to undesirable outcomes, because decision-makers must also account for the tail risk of decision quality. Prior risk-sensitive approaches typically model uncertainty explicitly and solve a stochastic or robust optimization problem at inference time, which increases computational complexity. We instead propose a DFL framework that achieves risk-sensitive behavior while retaining point predictions and deterministic optimization at inference time. Starting from the dual representation of the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) and adding entropy regularization, we derive a smooth surrogate for the CVaR of regret. Its gradient induces an instance-dependent reweighting within each minibatch that emphasizes high-risk outcomes, so the approach can turn existing surrogate-loss DFL methods, including the SPO+ loss, into risk-sensitive variants. When instantiated with SPO+, the resulting objective admits a generalization bound on the CVaR of the true regret. Experiments on knapsack, portfolio, shortest-path, and energy-aware scheduling problems show substantial reductions in tail regret when the uncertain parameters exhibit heterogeneous tail behavior.
core_methodology: A decision-focused learning (DFL) framework that incorporates Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to achieve risk-sensitive behavior while maintaining deterministic optimization at inference time. The method uses a smooth surrogate for CVaR of regret with entropy regularization, emphasizing high-risk outcomes through instance-dependent reweighting.
data_sources: Contextual information correlated with uncertain parameters in combinatorial optimization problems, applicable to portfolio optimization and other financial decision-making scenarios.
alpha_potential: The method can improve risk management in portfolio optimization and other financial applications by focusing on tail risk reduction, potentially leading to more robust decision-making under uncertainty.
title_cn: 风险规避的决策聚焦学习：最小化后悔的CVaR
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合条件风险价值（CVaR）的决策聚焦学习框架，通过熵正则化和实例相关重加权，在保持确定性优化的同时实现风险敏感行为。在投资组合优化等金融应用中，该方法可有效降低尾部风险，提升在不确定性下的决策稳健性。

title: SLiDE: Structured Linear Dynamics for Forecasting with Exogenous Inputs
summary: Accurate time series forecasting with exogenous inputs is critical across domains, including energy and retail, yet modern deep learning models often overfit to correlations that do not generalize under shifts in these inputs. We propose SLiDE, a Koopman-inspired architecture for forecasting with exogenous inputs that imposes structure on latent temporal dynamics. SLiDE approximates nonlinear system evolution using a learned linear operator in a latent space, combining (i) a history encoder that reconstructs the current latent state from past targets and inputs with (ii) a shared linear rollout driven by future exogenous variables. By enforcing a common linear recurrence across encoding and prediction, SLiDE aligns how past information is encoded with how future states evolve, reducing parameterization and preventing reliance on spurious correlations in the input history. Empirically, SLiDE achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on real-world benchmarks, including electricity price forecasting and retail demand, while maintaining a computational footprint comparable to lightweight MLP architectures. SLiDE is especially effective at generalizing to shifted exogenous inputs, reducing MSE by 20% on electricity price samples with out-of-range exogenous values and MAE by 30% in a synthetic transfer setting where the same dynamical system is driven by an unseen exogenous process. Ablations confirm the importance of both the structured history encoder and the linear latent rollout, suggesting that structured latent linear dynamics provide a useful inductive bias for forecasting with exogenous inputs.
core_methodology: SLiDE is a Koopman-inspired architecture that imposes structured linear dynamics in latent space for time series forecasting with exogenous inputs. It combines a history encoder for latent state reconstruction with a shared linear rollout driven by future exogenous variables, enforcing alignment between past encoding and future state evolution.
data_sources: Electricity price forecasting and retail demand data, with potential applicability to financial time series with exogenous inputs (e.g., macroeconomic indicators, news sentiment, or alternative data streams).
alpha_potential: The method's strength in handling shifted exogenous inputs and reducing reliance on spurious correlations could be valuable for financial forecasting where regime changes are common. Particularly useful for strategies dependent on external factors (e.g., commodity prices with macroeconomic drivers) or in environments with structural breaks.
title_cn: SLiDE：基于结构化线性动态的外生输入预测模型
summary_cn: SLiDE通过潜在空间中的结构化线性动态，结合历史编码器和外生变量驱动的线性展开，显著提升了含外生输入的时间序列预测性能。在金融领域，该方法特别适用于处理市场机制变化下的预测问题，如受宏观经济影响的资产价格预测，其抗外生变量偏移的特性可降低20-30%的预测误差。

title: FinVision: Multimodal AI for Visualizing Financial Narratives
summary: Financial narratives contain rich information about firms' performance and business conditions. Conventional text analysis often summarizes this information into numerical representations, which may not fully preserve the dynamic structure described in the narrative. In this study, we develop FinVision, a domain-specific multimodal generative model that translates financial narratives into visual representations of contemporaneous market dynamics. Using 87,940 paired observations of Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures and stock price charts, FinVision learns the average relationship between a firm's narrative account of a fiscal year and its stock-price dynamics over the same period. Given an MD&A alone, the trained model generates a text-implied stock chart, extending financial text analysis beyond numerical representations toward text-to-visual generation. We validate FinVision in two ways. First, held-out tests show that the model generates stock-chart representations that closely resemble observed charts and outperform direct LLM prompting, general-purpose text-to-image models, and the same architecture without financial-domain adaptation. Second, we examine the economic validity of the generated representations by comparing text-implied and observed stock charts. The resulting discrepancy is systematically associated with weaker investor responses around subsequent 10-K filings and with worse subsequent market and operating outcomes. Overall, our findings show how domain-adapted multimodal generative AI can create a new visual representation of financial text and provide an additional modality for studying business communication.
core_methodology: FinVision employs a domain-specific multimodal generative model to translate financial narratives (specifically MD&A disclosures) into visual representations of stock price charts. The model learns the relationship between textual narratives and contemporaneous stock price dynamics, enabling text-to-visual generation for financial analysis.
data_sources: The study uses 87,940 paired observations of Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures and corresponding stock price charts.
alpha_potential: The discrepancy between text-implied and observed stock charts is systematically associated with weaker investor responses and worse subsequent market outcomes, suggesting potential for identifying mispriced securities or predicting market reactions to financial disclosures.
title_cn: FinVision：用于可视化金融叙事的 multimodal AI
summary_cn: FinVision 是一种领域特定的多模态生成模型，能将财务叙事（如管理层讨论与分析）转化为股票价格走势的可视化表示。研究发现，文本隐含与实际股价图之间的差异与后续市场反应和公司业绩相关，为量化交易提供了新的信息提取方式和潜在 alpha 信号源。

title: Hierarchical Regime-Conditioned Dynamics for Spatiotemporal Graphs
summary: Forecasting the behavior of spatio-temporal systems often requires more than accurate predictions: models should uncover the dynamical modes governing future evolution. Existing temporal graph and latent dynamical models achieve strong forecasting performance, but their latent representations often entangle multiple dynamical patterns, limiting interpretability. Conversely, regime-inference methods explicitly model such modes but typically do not support generative forecasting over graph-structured systems. We introduce HERON, a self-supervised regime-aware generative framework that unifies graph-structured trajectory generation with regime identification. HERON factorizes the latent state into discrete system-level regimes, capturing global dynamical modes, and continuous entity-level dynamics, yielding a modular regime interface compatible with existing spatio-temporal backbones. Crucially, the inferred regime actively conditions system dynamics, enabling regime tracking and controlled simulations under alternative dynamical modes. Without regime annotations, HERON jointly learns forecasts and regime dynamics in a self-supervised manner, recovering meaningful modes across controlled synthetic and real-world datasets while maintaining competitive forecasting performance. These results open a path toward interpretable, controllable generative modeling of spatio-temporal dynamics.
core_methodology: HERON is a self-supervised regime-aware generative framework that combines graph-structured trajectory generation with regime identification. It factorizes the latent state into discrete system-level regimes and continuous entity-level dynamics, enabling interpretable and controllable modeling of spatio-temporal systems.
data_sources: The paper mentions controlled synthetic and real-world datasets, suggesting potential applicability to financial time series and market microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The ability to identify and track different market regimes could be valuable for regime-switching trading strategies, portfolio optimization, and risk management. The generative forecasting capability may also help in scenario analysis and stress testing.
title_cn: 时空图的分层状态条件动力学
summary_cn: HERON框架通过将潜在状态分解为离散的系统级状态和连续的实体级动态，实现了时空系统的可解释和可控建模。在量化交易中，该方法可用于识别市场状态、开发状态切换策略，并进行生成式市场情景分析，具有实际应用潜力。

title: Breaking feature collapse in self-supervised time series encoders
summary: General-purpose time series encoders promise a single backbone that generalises across tasks and domains; however, they currently do not scale. We trace this down to a critical point of failure: under the predominant masked data modelling supervision, the encoder's output tokens partially collapse. This is the natural consequence of supervising encoders only in the input space, which leaves no constraint against redundant token dimensions in the feature space. We introduce OTISv2, which suppresses the collapse by complementing the reconstruction objective in input space with two objectives in the feature space: a self-distillation loss against an exponential-moving-average teacher, and a KoLeo regulariser. Under matched training, the resulting encoder reduces the cosine similarity and lifts the effective rank of its output tokens relative to its predecessor, and it scales monotonically from 7.1 M to 116 M parameters where its predecessor declines. It matches or surpasses existing general-purpose time series encoders across 143 uni- and multi-variate datasets. To foster further research, we release our code and pre-trained weights.
core_methodology: The paper introduces OTISv2, a self-supervised time series encoder that addresses feature collapse by combining a reconstruction objective in input space with two feature space objectives: a self-distillation loss against an exponential-moving-average teacher and a KoLeo regulariser. This approach improves the diversity and effective rank of output tokens, enabling better scalability and performance across various time series datasets.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on 143 uni- and multi-variate datasets, which could include financial time series data such as stock prices, trading volumes, or other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The improved feature diversity and scalability of OTISv2 could enhance the extraction of meaningful patterns from financial time series data, potentially leading to better predictive models for trading signals, risk management, or portfolio optimization.
title_cn: 自监督时间序列编码器中的特征崩溃突破
summary_cn: 该论文提出的OTISv2通过结合输入空间的重建目标和特征空间的自蒸馏损失与KoLeo正则化，解决了自监督时间序列编码器中的特征崩溃问题。这一方法在金融时间序列分析中具有潜在应用价值，可提升交易信号预测和风险管理的模型性能。

title: Conformal Expert Pools: Training-Free Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting Beyond Seasonality
summary: Conformal Seasonal Pools (CSP) showed that a forecaster with no training at all, built only from past values at the same point in the season and from past forecast errors, significantly outperformed DeepNPTS, Amazon's learned non-parametric forecaster. We propose Conformal Expert Pools (CEP), a training-free successor. CEP replaces the single seasonal-naive forecast by a pool of simple forecasters, builds its predictive distribution from their past forecast errors, and adapts both the pool and the errors to the series being forecast. No model is trained and no parameter is learned across series. On the CSP benchmark of 232 datasets and 24,502 forecast windows, CEP is better than CSP on 78% of datasets by CRPS, on 84% by MSIS and on 83% by Winkler score; on a typical dataset its CRPS is 14% lower and its MSIS 23% lower (both p < 1e-22, paired Wilcoxon test), and coverage of 95% intervals rises from 90.1% to 92.2%. CEP has a lower CRPS than DeepNPTS on 88% of datasets, than NPTS on 89% and than SeasonalNPTS on 83%. The improvement persists on dataset families outside the development set and on 36 additional fev-bench files. We also test the published claims that Laplace, an online ensemble forecaster, "beats (almost) everything" and "beats" CSP. On 228 datasets at multi-step horizons the claims do not hold: CSP outperforms Laplace on 60% of datasets by CRPS and on 64% by interval score, and Laplace ranks sixth of seven methods, with the widest intervals of all (69% wider than CEP's). Its point forecast is biased low and on 54% of datasets is less accurate than seasonal naive, and from a cold start it takes about 7,700 times longer than CSP. CEP is better than Laplace on 82% of datasets by CRPS and on 80% by MSIS, with intervals about 40% narrower, and runs 271 times faster.
core_methodology: Conformal Expert Pools (CEP) is a training-free probabilistic time-series forecasting method that uses a pool of simple forecasters, builds predictive distributions from their past forecast errors, and adapts both the pool and the errors to the series being forecast. It requires no model training or parameter learning across series.
data_sources: Time-series data from 232 datasets and 24,502 forecast windows, including seasonal and non-seasonal patterns.
alpha_potential: CEP's ability to outperform learned forecasters like DeepNPTS and SeasonalNPTS suggests potential for generating alpha in markets with strong seasonal patterns or where simple, adaptive models can exploit recurring inefficiencies. Its probabilistic nature also allows for better risk management in trading strategies.
title_cn: 共形专家池：超越季节性的无训练概率时间序列预测
summary_cn: 共形专家池（CEP）是一种无需训练的概率时间序列预测方法，通过组合简单预测器并利用历史预测误差构建预测分布，在季节性数据上显著优于传统学习方法。该技术在金融时间序列预测中具有应用潜力，特别是在季节性明显的市场或需要快速适应的交易策略中。

title: The opposing informational effects of AI trading
summary: Better artificial intelligence (AI) can improve individual forecasts without making prices better at revealing new information. In a competitive market with resource-constrained forecasting, more capable algorithms can substitute analysis of public records for private observations, reducing the private information aggregated into prices. The same trades can convey sophisticated public-data analysis to investors unable to perform it themselves. We establish conditions under which these effects coexist and the private benefit of further computation falls. Numerical equilibrium calculations and finite-data neural-market experiments exhibit corresponding patterns. Out-of-sample earnings forecasts and controlled language-model tasks show related patterns of information substitution. In the neural experiment, wider adoption increases the predictive value of price for limited observers, reduces it for advanced observers, and lowers the benefit of upgrading by 44\%. Retraining by investors who did not upgrade can amplify the loss of private-information precision. The informational consequences of AI trading depend on what prices reveal and who can use them.
core_methodology: The paper examines the informational effects of AI trading in competitive markets through theoretical modeling, numerical equilibrium calculations, and neural-market experiments. It specifically analyzes how improved AI capabilities affect price discovery by shifting the balance between private information and public data analysis.
data_sources: The study uses both simulated market data (for numerical equilibrium calculations) and real-world out-of-sample earnings forecasts. It also includes controlled experiments with language models to validate the theoretical findings.
alpha_potential: The research identifies a counterintuitive effect where more sophisticated AI can reduce the private information aggregated into prices while simultaneously improving the informational content for less sophisticated investors. This creates potential alpha opportunities by understanding how different market participants process and react to AI-driven information flows.
title_cn: AI交易的信息对立效应
summary_cn: 本研究通过理论模型和神经市场实验发现，更先进的AI交易算法会改变市场价格发现机制：一方面减少私有信息在价格中的聚合，另一方面将复杂的公开数据分析传递给能力较弱的投资者。这种信息替代效应为理解AI时代市场微观结构变化提供了新视角，对开发基于信息不对称的量化策略具有重要启示。

title: FARCH: A Functional ARCH Model for Calibrated Prediction Bands
summary: Forecasting a curve, rather than a handful of scalar summaries of it, requires a notion of uncertainty that is itself functional. We propose FARCH, a functional nonlinear autoregressive model with conditional heteroscedasticity, in which the conditional mean and the conditional volatility of the next curve are forecasted jointly and nonparametrically, by reusing a single kernel weighting scheme --- built on a wavelet semi-metric between curves --- first on the curves themselves and then on their squared residuals. From this pair of estimators we derive two constructions of prediction bands: a pointwise band, obtained from marginal scenario quantiles, and a uniform, sup-norm band, calibrated for decisions that concern the entire forecasted path rather than any single instant. Applied to day-ahead forecasting of half-hourly French national electricity demand (1996--2009), and compared, under an identical protocol, against four existing prediction-interval constructions that do not model the conditional variance explicitly, the uniform FARCH band attains pointwise coverage statistically indistinguishable from its nominal target at the 80%, 90% and 95% levels, and a curve-wise coverage of 90.1%, significantly above the 70.8% reached by the best competing method, at the cost of a wider interval. Pointwise bands, in contrast, undercover regardless of whether the variance is modelled explicitly, indicating that state-dependent volatility and simultaneous calibration are two distinct ingredients that a trustworthy prediction band must combine.
core_methodology: Functional nonlinear autoregressive model with conditional heteroscedasticity (FARCH) for forecasting curves with functional uncertainty. It jointly forecasts conditional mean and volatility using a single kernel weighting scheme based on wavelet semi-metrics between curves.
data_sources: Half-hourly French national electricity demand data from 1996 to 2009.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to accurately forecast functional curves with calibrated uncertainty bands could be adapted for electricity price prediction and trading, particularly in markets with high volatility and complex temporal patterns. The uniform prediction bands offer potential for risk management in energy derivatives trading.
title_cn: FARCH：用于校准预测带的功能性ARCH模型
summary_cn: FARCH提出了一种功能性非线性自回归条件异方差模型，能够联合预测曲线的条件均值和条件波动性。通过对电力需求曲线的实证研究表明，该方法在统一预测带校准方面显著优于现有方法，为能源市场的波动性预测和风险管理提供了新的工具。

title: Contextual Causal Bayesian Optimisation
summary: We introduce a unified framework for contextual and causal Bayesian optimisation, which aims to design intervention policies maximising the expectation of a target variable. Our approach leverages both observed contextual information and known causal graph structures to guide the search. Within this framework, we propose a novel algorithm that jointly optimises over policies and the sets of variables on which these policies are defined. This thereby extends and unifies two previously distinct approaches: Causal Bayesian Optimisation and Contextual Bayesian Optimisation, while also addressing their limitations in scenarios that yield suboptimal results. We derive worst-case and instance-dependent high-probability regret bounds for our algorithm. We report experimental results across diverse environments, corroborating that our approach achieves sublinear regret and reduces sample complexity in high-dimensional settings.
core_methodology: A unified framework combining contextual and causal Bayesian optimization to design intervention policies that maximize the expectation of a target variable, leveraging both observed contextual information and known causal graph structures.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial datasets but the methodology is applicable to any structured financial data where causal relationships can be modeled (e.g., asset returns, macroeconomic indicators, order book data).
alpha_potential: The approach could identify optimal intervention points in trading strategies by modeling causal relationships between market factors, potentially uncovering non-obvious relationships that generate alpha. Particularly relevant for factor timing, smart order routing, or portfolio rebalancing strategies.
title_cn: 情境因果贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合情境信息和因果结构的贝叶斯优化框架，可应用于金融市场的策略优化。通过同时优化策略变量集和干预政策，该方法能有效发现市场因子间的因果关系，为组合再平衡、因子择时等量化策略提供理论支持，实验证明在高维环境下具有样本效率优势。

title: Data-Driven Exploration for a Class of Continuous-Time Indefinite Linear--Quadratic Reinforcement Learning Problems
summary: We study reinforcement learning (RL) for a class of continuous-time stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) control problems, where volatilities depend on both states and controls while states are scalar-valued and there are no running control rewards, the last feature also leading to the so-called indefinite LQ controls. We propose a model-free, data-driven exploration mechanism that adaptively adjusts entropy regularization by the critic and policy variance by the actor. Unlike the constant or deterministic exploration schedules employed in the existing literature, which require extensive tuning for implementations and ignore learning progress during iterations, our adaptive exploratory approach boosts learning efficiency with minimal tuning. Despite its flexibility, our method achieves a sublinear regret bound that matches the best-known model-free results for this class of LQ problems, which were previously derived only with fixed exploration schedules. Numerical experiments demonstrate that adaptive explorations accelerate convergence and improve regret performance compared to the non-adaptive model-free and model-based counterparts.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an adaptive exploration mechanism for reinforcement learning in the context of continuous-time stochastic linear-quadratic control problems. It uses an actor-critic framework with adaptive entropy regularization and policy variance to enhance learning efficiency.
data_sources: The methodology is model-free and data-driven, but the abstract does not specify particular financial data sources. It is implied that any continuous-time financial data could be used.
alpha_potential: The adaptive exploration approach could potentially lead to better reinforcement learning policies for algorithmic trading strategies, particularly in environments requiring continuous-time adaptation and risk management. The sublinear regret bound suggests improved performance over non-adaptive methods.
title_cn: 数据驱动的一类连续时间不定线性二次强化学习问题探索
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种用于连续时间随机线性二次控制问题的自适应探索强化学习算法。通过动态调整探索策略，该方法能更高效地学习交易策略，在算法交易中具有潜在应用价值，特别是对于需要连续时间风险管理的交易环境。

title: Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit: A Unified Framework of Best Arm Identification and Regret Minimization for Dueling Bandits
summary: We study $N$-armed stochastic dueling bandits under the Condorcet-winner assumption with a positive global gap, where three widely adopted objectives are considered: best-arm identification (BAI), weak regret, and strong regret. We propose Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit (TG-ITE), the first unified framework to tackle all these objectives to our knowledge. Without requiring transitivity assumptions, we propose a shared tree-guided identification approach to find a high-confidence incumbent within $O(N)$ comparisons. We further propose varied exploitation strategies to utilize this warm-start stage to optimize the specific objectives at hand. For a fixed global gap $\Delta$, this methodology enables our approach to (1) build the first winner-stays-style algorithm to achieve $O(N)$ weak regret; (2) realize the joint optimization of BAI and weak regret with $O(N)$ guarantees for both, eliminating the sub-optimal $O(\log N)$ factors of the existing approach; (3) attain the same $O(N\log T)$ order as specialized strong-regret approaches; and (4) achieve $O(N)$ sample complexity in BAI, matching a worst-case lower bound up to an additional $\log(1/\Delta)$ term. If a lower bound on the minimal winner gap is known, this term can be removed. Our results suggest that a single identification primitive can serve BAI and both regret objectives with linear dependence on $N$.
core_methodology: Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit (TG-ITE) framework for dueling bandits, combining best-arm identification and regret minimization techniques without requiring transitivity assumptions.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any stochastic environment where pairwise comparisons can be made, such as stock pairs or trading strategies.
alpha_potential: Potential for identifying optimal trading strategies or portfolio allocations through pairwise comparisons, with applications in strategy selection and adaptive trading systems.
title_cn: 树引导的识别后利用：对决赌博机中最佳臂识别和遗憾最小化的统一框架
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的TG-ITE框架，能够在对决赌博机设置中同时优化最佳策略识别和遗憾最小化。通过树状引导方法在不需传递性假设的情况下快速确定优势策略，该技术可应用于交易策略优化和自适应投资组合管理，特别适合需要频繁策略调整的高频交易环境。

title: Short Windows, Unmodelled Costs, Unknown Cutoffs: A Pre-Registered Evidence Audit of 91 LLM Trading Papers
summary: Papers on large-language-model (LLM) trading agents and alpha mining report Sharpe ratios that would be remarkable in any other part of empirical finance. We audit the evidence behind those numbers. Before coding a single paper we pre-registered a population of 91 papers from a curated corpus of LLM trading research, a ten-field coding rubric, an analysis script and five directional hypotheses, and committed all of them to version control. Every code is backed by a verbatim quote that a script checks against the paper's text, and a second, blind coder recoded a random 20%. Of the 75 papers with a trading test, 51% deduct no trading costs and only 9% model costs from data; the median test window is 12 months, and a quarter of windows are six months or shorter. Among the 51 papers whose test window is not known to lie after the model's training cutoff, 98% neither test after the cutoff, nor evaluate live, nor use a chronologically consistent model. Only 9% report a multiplicity-adjusted result, and just five papers combine deducted costs, a leakage control and a reported trial count. Two of the five hypotheses pass (short windows; uncontrolled look-ahead). Three fail: more papers report a trial count than we predicted, though most of those counts are repeated random seeds rather than the number of strategies searched; and the predicted links between headline Sharpe and test-window length, and between headline Sharpe and costs, are not detectable in the 13 papers that state a headline Sharpe in their abstract or conclusion. We release the codes, quotes and script, and propose a six-line reporting minimum.
core_methodology: Systematic evidence audit of 91 LLM trading papers using pre-registered coding rubric and blind recoding for validation. Focuses on evaluating the robustness of reported Sharpe ratios by examining trading costs, test window lengths, and look-ahead bias controls.
data_sources: Academic papers on LLM trading agents and alpha mining from a curated corpus of LLM trading research.
alpha_potential: Highlights critical flaws in current LLM trading research that could lead to inflated performance metrics. Provides methodology to identify more reliable strategies by focusing on proper cost accounting, adequate test windows, and leakage controls.
title_cn: 短窗口、未建模成本、未知截止点：对91篇LLM交易论文的预注册证据审计
summary_cn: 本研究对91篇LLM交易论文进行了系统审计，发现多数研究存在测试窗口过短（中位数12个月）、未扣除交易成本（51%）、未控制前瞻性偏差（98%）等问题。提出了六项最低报告标准，为量化交易领域识别可靠的LLM策略提供了重要方法论。

title: A Second Order Transport Scheme for Dynamic Portfolio Subspaces under a Varying Risk Metric
summary: We analyze the transport of portfolio exposures between moving subspaces under a varying positive definite risk metric. The reference evolution is the induced connection obtained from the ambient connection of minimum norm in fixed asset coordinates. An explicit expansion of risk weighted Procrustes identifies a leading local error that couples metric deformation with covariant motion normal to the subspace. A rank two construction with an exact continuous solution shows that this term can reduce global accuracy to first order even when the metric commutes with its derivative. Geometric mean alignment and a symmetric Procrustes construction cancel the term and yield reversible updates with second order global accuracy. We establish uniform error bounds on nonuniform partitions, characterize the cases in which the Procrustes defect vanishes, and distinguish discretization error from errors in estimated geometry. We also characterize the connection induced by principal square root whitening and its relation to the selected transport. Manufactured examples confirm the predicted defect and convergence rates. A historical geometry stress test then estimates the defect from preceding observations and finds that it predicts the subsequent separation between risk weighted Procrustes and both second order updates, while the two second order schemes remain much closer to each other. Portfolio comparisons separately evaluate target persistence, turnover, and economic implementation.
core_methodology: The paper presents a second-order transport scheme for dynamic portfolio subspaces under varying risk metrics, utilizing risk-weighted Procrustes analysis and geometric mean alignment to improve accuracy in portfolio updates.
data_sources: Likely uses historical asset returns and risk metrics derived from market data, as suggested by the mention of a historical geometry stress test.
alpha_potential: The method could enhance dynamic portfolio optimization by better handling time-varying risk metrics, potentially improving risk-adjusted returns through more accurate exposure adjustments.
title_cn: 可变风险度量下动态投资组合子空间的二阶传输方案
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种在时变风险度量下动态调整投资组合子空间的二阶传输方案，通过风险加权Procrustes分析和几何均值对齐方法提高组合调整的精度。该方法在历史回测中显示出显著降低误差，并能预测后续风险调整差异，适合需要动态风险管理的量化策略。

title: SAiFE-gym: Model-based Environments for Automated Market Making with Concentrated Liquidity
summary: We present SAiFE_gym, a Python module that provides a collection of simulation environments for studying trading problems in constant product markets (CPMs) with concentrated liquidity (CL). These markets give liquidity providers (LPs) granular control over how their capital is allocated and enable them to adjust their range of liquidity provision dynamically based on market conditions, which in turn determines how they earn fees. We decompose the microstructure of CPMs with CL into interactive components that allow researchers and practitioners to capture various economic settings. We employ a vectorized approach to optimize our environments, making them scalable for high-dimensional reinforcement learning (RL) workflows, suitable for learning dynamic liquidity provision strategies. We demonstrate the benefits of our environments by evaluating the performance of RL agents in CPMs with CL under various market conditions.
core_methodology: The paper presents a Python module (SAiFE_gym) that offers simulation environments for studying trading problems in constant product markets (CPMs) with concentrated liquidity (CL). It employs a vectorized approach to optimize these environments for high-dimensional reinforcement learning (RL) workflows, enabling the development of dynamic liquidity provision strategies.
data_sources: The paper focuses on simulated environments for constant product markets (CPMs) with concentrated liquidity, which are common in decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms like Uniswap v3.
alpha_potential: The methodology allows for the development of dynamic liquidity provision strategies that can adapt to market conditions, potentially capturing fee income more efficiently in decentralized exchanges. This could lead to improved returns for liquidity providers by optimizing their capital allocation based on real-time market data.
title_cn: SAiFE-gym：基于模型的集中流动性自动做市环境
summary_cn: SAiFE_gym是一个Python模块，提供了一系列模拟环境，用于研究具有集中流动性的恒定乘积市场中的交易问题。该模块采用向量化方法优化环境，适用于高维强化学习工作流，可帮助开发动态流动性提供策略。这对于在去中心化金融（DeFi）平台中优化做市策略具有实际应用价值。

title: Principal component error in high-dimensional factor models
summary: In a statistical factor model, principal components (or eigenvectors) of a sample covariance matrix serve as estimates of principal directions, the true drivers of co-movement of a collection of observed variables. We write the often substantial error in these estimates as a sum of two interpretable terms, which we show have almost sure asymptotic limits as the number of variables grows with sample size bounded. This scenario is commonplace in financial economics, genomics, machine learning and signal processing. Out-of-subspace error measures the distance from an estimate to the subspace spanned by population factor exposures. It can be expressed in terms of data, providing an estimable floor for asymptotic error. In-subspace error is driven by a rotation error within that subspace, which arises from the fixed sample size of the latent factor returns and cannot be estimated from data alone. We illustrate our error analysis with a three-factor simulation of the US public equity market, showing the dependence of the magnitude of the error and its components on dimension and sample size. In that simulation, out-of-subspace error dominates. Researchers who rely on principal component analysis to estimate factor models can use our results to quantify errors in model-based predictions and attributions.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the error in principal component analysis (PCA) estimates of factor models, decomposing it into out-of-subspace and in-subspace error components. It provides asymptotic limits and practical methods to quantify these errors in high-dimensional settings.
data_sources: The paper uses US public equity market data for its simulation, though the methodology is applicable to any high-dimensional financial dataset.
alpha_potential: By quantifying and decomposing PCA estimation errors, this research can improve factor model accuracy in portfolio construction and risk attribution. It directly addresses a key limitation in factor investing strategies.
title_cn: 高维因子模型中主成分误差分析
summary_cn: 该论文创新性地将因子模型中的主成分估计误差分解为子空间外误差和子空间内误差，建立了误差的渐进极限并提供了量化方法。对于依赖主成分分析的公募股票因子投资策略，该研究可显著改善风险归因和组合优化的准确性，尤其适用于高维金融数据场景。

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Mambas Selective Gate in Financial Markets: A Leakage-Controlled Study
summary: Selectively gated state-space models (SSMs), notably Mamba, are increasingly used for financial time series, yet how they internally represent market regimes (bull, bear, sideways) remains opaque. This paper applies Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) to a six-layer Mamba trained on approximately twenty-one years of daily data for a point-in-time set of S&P 500 constituents plus macroeconomic and Fama-French factors, decomposing per-layer hidden states with Top-K Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs). Our central contribution is methodological and cautionary. A prior, uncontrolled configuration recovered market regimes from SAE features at F1 = 1.00. Under a controlled protocol that (i) removes the three input features that overlap the HMM label definition, (ii) disables the auxiliary regime-classification head, (iii) uses a point-in-time constituent universe, and (iv) evaluates against labels disjoint from the inputs, the same regime label is recovered at only F1 = 0.398, indistinguishable from a logistic baseline on raw inputs (0.435) and from an SAE trained on a randomly initialized, untrained Mamba (0.364). A 2x2 attribution grid shows the near-perfect result is an interaction of auxiliary supervision and label-defining inputs: neither factor alone exceeds F1 ~ 0.40. Effect sizes with block-bootstrap inference show the residual selective-gate (Delta t) regime effect is statistically detectable but economically negligible and uniform across layers rather than layer-specialized; the apparent polysemanticity gradient disappears under continuous, theory-grounded measures. We contribute a reproducible leakage-control protocol for interpretability evaluation of financial SSMs, a quantified demonstration that previously reported regime structure is a label-contamination artifact, and a modest economically grounded feature subset that genuinely survives the controls.
core_methodology: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) applied to Mamba's selective gated state-space model (SSM) with Top-K Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to study market regime representation, incorporating a leakage-control protocol
data_sources: 21 years of daily data for S&P 500 constituents plus macroeconomic and Fama-French factors, using a point-in-time universe
alpha_potential: The study reveals that previously reported regime structures were artifacts of label contamination. It identifies a modest, economically grounded feature subset that survives rigorous controls, suggesting limited but detectable regime effects in SSMs
title_cn: 金融市场中Mamba选择性门的机制可解释性研究：泄漏控制分析
summary_cn: 本研究应用机制可解释性技术，分析六层Mamba模型在标普500成分股21年数据中的市场状态表示。核心贡献在于开发了泄漏控制协议，证明先前报告的机制结构是标签污染的假象。研究发现选择性门对市场状态的影响虽可检测但经济意义微弱，为量化模型在真实市场环境中的可靠性提供了重要方法论验证。

title: When Helpful Agents Cause Financial Harm: Evaluating LLM Agent Safety in Executable Economic Worlds
summary: As LLM agents become increasingly capable of making consequential economic decisions, their safety under economic pressures remains poorly understood. We introduce EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety of LLM agents in executable economic environments. EconSafeBench contains 828 cases across five economic scenarios and four categories of safety violations. A key design is the matched evaluation of three sources of safety pressure, including explicit user requests, pressure from other actors, and pressure arising from the agent's own pursuit of a performance objective. We further evaluate safety at both static and dynamic scales through 30-period interactions with persistent memory and matched controls. Across eight LLMs, all evaluated models exhibit safety violations on the static benchmark, with overall violation rates ranging from 8.5% to 40.6%. We further find that violations can occur even without an explicit unsafe request, and that initially compliant agents may begin to violate as performance pressure increases over time. These findings highlight the need for stronger safety alignment and rigorous evaluation before LLM agents are deployed in high-stakes economic environments.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a benchmark (EconSafeBench) for evaluating the safety of LLM agents in economic environments through 828 test cases across five scenarios, focusing on three sources of safety pressure: explicit user requests, pressure from other actors, and performance objectives.
data_sources: The study uses simulated economic environments (executable economic worlds) to test LLM behaviors, rather than real financial market data.
alpha_potential: While not directly generating trading signals, the research highlights risks in deploying LLM agents for economic decision-making, which is crucial for ensuring safety in automated trading systems and financial applications using LLMs.
title_cn: 当辅助代理造成财务损害：评估可执行经济世界中的LLM代理安全性
summary_cn: 论文提出EconSafeBench基准，首次系统评估可执行经济环境中LLM代理的安全性，涵盖五种经济场景和四类安全违规。研究发现所有测试模型在静态基准下均存在8.5%-40.6%的违规率，且在绩效压力下合规代理可能转为违规。这对金融领域部署LLM代理的风险管控具有重要参考价值。

title: Stagewise Adaptive Boosting
summary: Stagewise algorithms and sparsity-inducing regularization are two influential approaches to high-dimensional modeling. Existing stagewise theory, however, largely centers on convex regularization, whereas stronger sparsity and other structural preferences are often pursued through fixed-level nonconvex optimization rather than generating an entire adaptive solution path. We develop stagewise adaptive boosting, a general framework that builds a monotone path by selecting the update consistent with structural preference. The framework can encourage sparsity along the path itself and also admits extensions that promote other properties of the solution, including group selection, similarity across models for multiple outcomes, and known priorities or prerequisite relations among predictors. We study its theoretical property as well as finite sample performance using simulations and real-data analyses. Across these studies, the proposed pathwise approach often achieves predictive performance comparable to commonly used baselines while selecting substantially smaller models. These results suggest that adaptive stagewise learning provides a practical route to stronger sparsity and richer structural control without repeatedly solving separate weighted or nonconvex optimization problems.
core_methodology: Stagewise adaptive boosting, a framework for building monotone paths in high-dimensional modeling with structural preferences like sparsity, group selection, and predictor priorities.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but applicable to any high-dimensional financial data (e.g., stock returns, macroeconomic indicators).
alpha_potential: Potential for creating sparse, interpretable models in factor investing or portfolio optimization, possibly leading to more robust strategies with fewer predictors.
title_cn: 阶段性自适应提升
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种阶段性自适应提升框架，适用于高维金融数据建模，能够生成稀疏且结构化的解决方案路径。在量化交易中，该方法可能用于开发更简洁、更稳健的因子投资策略或投资组合优化模型，减少过拟合风险并提高模型可解释性。

title: Setting Optimal Reserve Prices using Fine-Tuned Language Models
summary: Online auction houses must set reserve prices for highly differentiated products whose unstructured descriptions contain valuable demand information. Existing approaches generally require managers to specify product attributes in advance.
